subject: cs-9
description: Evolution of computing, generations, system components, Von Neumann architecture, CPU buses, primary & secondary storage, and I/O devices.

questions.question: Which early computing device used beads on rods to perform arithmetic?
questions.explanation: The Abacus is one of the oldest computing tools, using beads on rods for arithmetic. It was widely used across many ancient cultures long before mechanical calculators.

questions.question: Who invented the Difference Engine in the 1820s?
questions.explanation: Charles Babbage designed the Difference Engine in the 1820s for mechanical numerical computation. He is often called the “Father of the Computer.”

questions.question: The Tabulating Machine invented by Herman Hollerith laid the foundation for which company?
questions.explanation: Hollerith’s punch card-based machine was so successful that his company eventually evolved into IBM (International Business Machines Corporation).

questions.question: First Generation computers used which core technology?
questions.explanation: First Generation (1940–1956) computers used vacuum tubes — large, fragile glass components that made machines enormous, power-hungry, and unreliable.

questions.question: Which high-level programming languages were introduced in the Second Generation?
questions.explanation: Second Generation computers introduced FORTRAN (scientific use) and COBOL (business use) — the first widely used high-level languages replacing assembly code.

questions.question: Integrated Circuits (ICs) were the defining technology of which generation?
questions.explanation: Third Generation (1963–1971) used ICs — single chips holding multiple transistors — making computers significantly smaller, faster, and more reliable.

questions.question: Which generation of computers introduced the microprocessor?
questions.explanation: The Fourth Generation (1971–present) saw the development of microprocessors using LSI and VLSI technologies — integrating an entire CPU onto one chip.

questions.question: The world’s first microprocessor, the Intel 4004, was introduced in:
questions.explanation: Intel invented the world’s first microprocessor — the Intel 4004 — in November 1971, marking the beginning of the Fourth Generation of computers.

questions.question: Fifth Generation computers focus primarily on:

options.B: Artificial Intelligence and Natural Language Processing

questions.explanation: Fifth Generation computing centers on AI and NLP — enabling machines to learn, reason, and understand human language autonomously.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a First Generation computer?
questions.explanation: UNIVAC I was one of the earliest commercial computers using vacuum tubes — a classic First Generation machine. CDC 6600 is Third Generation; Intel Pentium is Fourth.

questions.question: Mark I computer, built in 1944 by Howard Aiken, was capable of:

options.C: Adding three 8-digit numbers per second using electric switches

questions.explanation: Mark I was an electromechanical computer that used electric switches and relays to perform calculations, printing outputs on cards or paper tape.

questions.question: Napier’s Bones, invented by John Napier, was primarily used to simplify:
questions.explanation: Napier’s Bones used numbered strips to simplify multiplication and division. Napier also introduced the decimal point system. Topic 1.2 — Natural vs Artificial Systems

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a NATURAL system?
questions.explanation: The human body is a natural biological system. Power grids, the internet, and robots are all artificial systems designed and built by humans.

questions.question: Artificial systems differ from natural systems because they:

options.B: Are governed by natural laws like physics
options.C: Are designed by humans to fulfill specific needs
options.D: Use solar energy as their power source

questions.explanation: Artificial systems are intentionally created by humans with specific purposes. Natural systems occur organically without human design or intervention.

questions.question: Which characteristic is TRUE of natural systems but NOT artificial systems?
questions.explanation: Natural systems like ecosystems adapt and evolve through natural processes without human involvement. Artificial systems need humans to redesign or update them.

questions.question: A computer network is classified as:
questions.explanation: A computer network is intentionally designed and built by humans. It requires maintenance and uses artificial energy — making it a classic artificial system.

questions.question: Which energy source do natural systems primarily rely on?

options.C: Natural sources like sunlight and water

questions.explanation: Natural systems use naturally available energy sources such as sunlight, water, and wind — unlike artificial systems that typically require electricity or fuel.

questions.question: A forest ecosystem is an example of:

options.B: A natural system with self-regulating components
options.C: A hybrid system designed by humans

questions.explanation: Forests are natural ecosystems that self- regulate through natural processes like photosynthesis, predator-prey balance, and seasonal adaptation.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a system?

options.A: A single component performing one task
options.B: A collection of interconnected components working together to achieve specific goals
options.C: A program stored on a computer
options.D: A hardware device connected to a network

questions.explanation: A system is defined as interconnected components that work together to process inputs and produce desired outputs toward a common goal. Topic 1.3.1 & 1.3.2 — Input Devices & System Unit

questions.question: Which input device converts sound into digital signals?
questions.explanation: A microphone converts sound (analog) into digital signals for use in voice commands, video calls, and audio recording applications.

questions.question: The “brain” of a computer that executes instructions is called:
questions.explanation: The microprocessor (CPU) is considered the brain of the computer. It executes instructions and performs arithmetic and logical operations.

questions.question: Which component of the CPU handles mathematical operations and logical comparisons?
questions.explanation: The ALU handles all mathematical operations (addition, subtraction) and logical comparisons (greater than, equal to) within the CPU.

questions.question: The Control Unit (CU) in a CPU is responsible for:

options.C: Managing and directing the execution of instructions
options.D: Connecting the CPU to output devices

questions.explanation: The Control Unit manages the sequence of operations, directing data flow and coordinating all system activities without performing calculations itself.

questions.question: A barcode reader is most commonly used in which setting?
questions.explanation: Barcode readers scan product barcodes to extract price, inventory, and product details — making them essential in retail checkout and supply chain management.

questions.question: The motherboard serves as the:

options.B: Backbone of the computer ensuring communication between all parts

questions.explanation: The motherboard is the main circuit board that connects and enables communication between the CPU, memory, storage, and all other components.

questions.question: What makes a touch screen different from other input devices?

options.A: It only works with a stylus
options.B: It combines both input and output functionalities
options.D: It can only be used on desktops

questions.explanation: A touch screen acts as both an input device (detecting touch gestures) and output device (displaying information) simultaneously.

questions.question: Registers in the CPU are used to:

options.A: Store data permanently for long-term use
options.B: Hold data and instructions temporarily during processing
options.C: Connect the CPU to external devices

questions.explanation: Registers are the fastest and smallest storage inside the CPU, holding data and instructions only for the immediate duration of processing. Topic 1.3.3 & 1.3.4 — Storage & Output Devices

questions.question: What makes SSDs faster than traditional Hard Disk Drives (HDDs)?

options.C: SSDs use ICs with no moving parts

questions.explanation: SSDs store data in integrated circuit chips with no mechanical movement. HDDs use spinning magnetic platters and mechanical read/write heads, making them slower.

questions.question: Which storage device has a capacity of 700MB and uses optical technology?
questions.explanation: A CD has a standard capacity of 700MB and uses laser technology to read/write data. DVDs hold more (up to 16GB) and USB drives vary widely.

questions.question: Which output device is most suitable for printing large-scale engineering blueprints?
questions.explanation: Plotters are designed specifically for printing large-scale graphics like engineering drawings, maps, and banners on large sheets of paper.

questions.question: Dot matrix printers are classified as:
questions.explanation: Dot matrix printers are impact printers — they use mechanical pins to strike an ink ribbon onto paper. Laser and inkjet printers are non-impact.

questions.question: A USB Flash Drive connects to a computer via:
questions.explanation: USB Flash Drives are portable storage devices that connect through USB (Universal Serial Bus) ports, offering easy plug-and-play data transfer.

questions.question: Which output device converts digital audio signals into sound?
questions.explanation: Speakers are output devices that convert digital audio signals from the computer into sound waves for music, video, gaming, and multimedia.

questions.question: DVD stands for:
questions.explanation: DVD stands for Digital Versatile Disk. It has a larger storage capacity than a CD (up to 16GB) and is suitable for multimedia content like movies.

questions.question: Which storage device is most suitable for a photographer transferring photos from a camera to a laptop?
questions.explanation: Memory cards are small portable storage devices used in cameras and smartphones. They easily transfer photos to laptops via a card reader. Topic 1.3.5 & 1.4 — Expansion Slots/Cards & Von Neumann Architecture

questions.question: Von Neumann Architecture was first published in:
questions.explanation: John Von Neumann published his architecture concept in 1945. It introduced the stored- program concept that is still the basis of most modern computers.

questions.question: The stored-program concept in Von Neumann Architecture means:

options.A: Programs are stored on external USB devices only
options.B: Instructions and data are stored in the same memory
options.C: Each program requires its own separate memory chip
options.D: Programs are hardwired into the CPU

questions.explanation: Von Neumann’s key innovation was storing both program instructions and data in the same memory, allowing programs to be loaded and changed without hardware modification.

questions.question: Which bus carries memory ADDRESSES between the processor and memory?
questions.explanation: The Address Bus carries the addresses (locations) of data — not the data itself — between the CPU and memory, telling the system where to read or write.

questions.question: The Control Bus in a computer system is responsible for:

options.A: Carrying data between CPU and memory
options.B: Carrying memory addresses to the processor
options.C: Carrying control signals to coordinate all computer activities
options.D: Connecting input devices to the CPU

questions.explanation: The Control Bus carries commands and control signals from the CPU to coordinate and manage all activities within the computer system.

questions.question: Expansion slots on a motherboard are used to:

options.B: Install additional hardware cards to expand system functionality
options.C: Connect the computer to the internet
options.D: Control the speed of the CPU

questions.explanation: Expansion slots are sockets on the motherboard where circuit boards (like graphics cards, sound cards, network cards) can be inserted to add capabilities.

questions.question: The I/O Controller in Von Neumann Architecture manages:

options.B: Data flow between the CPU and external devices like hard drives and USB

questions.explanation: The I/O Controller acts as an interface managing data transfer between the CPU/memory and external peripheral devices.

questions.question: A network card installed in an expansion slot is an example of:
questions.explanation: Expansion cards (like network cards, graphics cards, sound cards) are circuit boards inserted into expansion slots to add or enhance computer functionality.

questions.question: Why is Von Neumann Architecture still widely used today?

options.A: It is the cheapest architecture to build
options.B: It supports only machine language programming
options.C: Its stored-program concept is flexible and efficient for general-purpose computing
options.D: It does not require a CPU

questions.explanation: The ability to store and change programs in memory without hardware changes makes Von Neumann Architecture highly flexible and practical for all modern computers. Topic 1.1 & 1.6 — System Buses, CPU & Memory

questions.question: Which bus in a computer carries data between the CPU and memory?
questions.explanation: The Data Bus carries actual data between CPU, memory, and I/O devices. The Address Bus carries memory addresses and the Control Bus manages signals.

questions.question: What is the correct order of the fetch-decode-execute cycle?
questions.explanation: The CPU always fetches the instruction first, decodes it to understand it, then executes it. This cycle repeats continuously.

questions.question: Which type of memory loses its content when the computer is switched off?
questions.explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) is volatile — it requires constant power to retain data. ROM, Flash, and Hard Disk are non-volatile.

questions.question: What is the role of cache memory in a computer system?

options.C: To speed up CPU access to frequently used data
options.D: To connect devices to the CPU

questions.explanation: Cache memory stores frequently used instructions/data closer to the CPU for faster access, reducing the time the CPU waits.

questions.question: A computer's BIOS is stored in which type of memory?
questions.explanation: BIOS is stored in ROM (Read-Only Memory) because it must persist even without power and is not changed during normal use.

questions.question: Which secondary memory uses laser beams to read and write data?
questions.explanation: Optical media like DVDs use laser technology. SSDs and Flash Drives use flash memory, while HDDs use magnetic platters.

questions.question: What does pipelining do in a CPU?

options.B: Allows multiple instruction stages to overlap

questions.explanation: Pipelining overlaps fetch, decode and execute stages of different instructions to increase throughput and CPU efficiency.

questions.question: Which memory type sits at the TOP of the memory hierarchy (closest to CPU)?
questions.explanation: Registers are the fastest and smallest memory, directly inside the CPU — they sit at the very top of the hierarchy.

questions.question: Interrupts in a CPU are used to:

options.B: Allow the CPU to respond to external events by pausing current tasks

questions.explanation: An interrupt signal causes the CPU to save its current state and handle the interrupt (e.g. keyboard press) before resuming.

questions.question: What determines the width of the address bus?
questions.explanation: A 32-bit address bus can address 2^32 memory locations. Wider address buses allow more memory to be addressed. Topic 1.6.5 & 1.7 — Secondary Memory, Software & Hardware Engineering

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of chip-based secondary memory?
questions.explanation: SSDs (Solid State Drives) use flash memory chips with no moving parts. HDDs use magnetic disks and CDs use optical technology.

questions.question: Software engineering that focuses on programs built into devices like microwaves is called:
questions.explanation: Embedded software is designed specifically for hardware devices with dedicated functions. It is not intended for general use.

questions.question: Hardware engineering that deals with designing CPUs and logic circuits is:
questions.explanation: Digital hardware engineers work with binary (0s and 1s) and design components like CPUs, GPUs, and logic gates.

questions.question: Which of the following is system software?
questions.explanation: An OS is system software that manages hardware and provides a platform for applications. The others are application software.

questions.question: Why does a hard disk have slower access speed than RAM?
questions.explanation: HDD uses spinning magnetic platters and a mechanical read/write head, making it inherently slower than electronic RAM.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an assembler in programming?

options.A: To convert high-level code to machine code
options.B: To translate assembly language to machine code

questions.explanation: An assembler converts assembly language (low-level mnemonics) into machine code (binary). A compiler converts high-level languages.

questions.question: Which type of programming language is closest to hardware and hardest to read?
questions.explanation: Machine language consists of binary (0s and 1s) and is directly understood by the CPU, but extremely difficult for humans to read.

questions.question: Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) is best suited for:

options.B: Managing complex programs using objects and classes

questions.explanation: OOP organizes code into objects and classes, making it easier to manage large, complex software systems through encapsulation and reuse.

questions.question: Device drivers are a type of:
questions.explanation: Device drivers are system software that allow the OS to communicate with hardware devices like printers, keyboards, and graphics cards.

questions.question: Which is NOT a function of an Operating System?
questions.explanation: The OS manages memory, files, and processes. Web page design is done using application-level tools like HTML editors. Topic 1.9 — Data Communication, OSI Model & Protocols

questions.question: Which mode of communication allows data to flow in BOTH directions simultaneously?
questions.explanation: Full-Duplex allows simultaneous two-way communication (e.g. phone calls). Half- Duplex is turn-based (e.g. walkie-talkies), Simplex is one-way.

questions.question: A walkie-talkie uses which mode of data communication?
questions.explanation: Walkie-talkies transmit in one direction at a time — one person speaks while the other listens, then they switch. This is Half-Duplex.

questions.question: In asynchronous transmission, which bits are used to frame each character?
questions.explanation: Asynchronous transmission uses start bits (to signal beginning) and stop bits (to signal end) for each character sent independently.

questions.question: The OSI model has how many layers?
questions.explanation: The OSI model has 7 layers: Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link, and Physical.

questions.question: Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for routing packets across networks?
questions.explanation: The Network Layer (Layer 3) handles routing of data packets between different networks. IP addressing operates at this layer.

questions.question: HTTP is used for:
questions.explanation: HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is used by web browsers to request and display web pages. It operates at the Application layer.

questions.question: FTP stands for:
questions.explanation: FTP (File Transfer Protocol) is used to transfer files between a client and server over a network.

questions.question: Which network topology uses a single central cable to connect all devices?
questions.explanation: Bus topology uses one main cable (backbone) to which all devices connect. Failure of the backbone affects the whole network.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of Packet Switching over Circuit Switching?

options.B: Dedicated path between sender and receiver

questions.explanation: Packet Switching breaks data into packets that can take different routes, making better use of available bandwidth than dedicated circuit paths.

questions.question: SMTP is primarily used for:
questions.explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is used to send emails from a client to a mail server and between mail servers.
